--- title: "Suitable locations for potential aquaculture" description: "Mapping U.S west coast for species" affiliation: - University of California, Santa Barbara - Masters of Environmental Data Science at the Bren School affiliation-url: https://bren.ucsb.edu/masters-programs/master-environmental-data-science date: 12-02-2026 format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" categories: [Aquaculture, Data Science, Geospatial, R] image: images/aqua.jpg editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline --- # Background Marine aquaculture have the potential to be a more sustainable option than the alternative land-based meat for the global food supply (Hall et al, 2011). Gentry et al. created a map based on the neccessay constraints for marine aquaculture including, ship traffics, dissolved oxygen, and bottom depth, concluding that the global seafood demand could be met with less than 0.015% of the global ocean area. The main goal is to create a function that will input the following: minimum and maximum sea surface temp, minimum and maximum depth, and the species name. The output will be a map of the EEZ regions colored by the amount of suitable areas for the selected species. **Which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) is suitable for aquaculture?** The approach to find suitable locations will be determined based on the range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species, both oysters and blue mussels. # Are marine aquaculutres impactful in sustainability? A recent study from the UN shows that aquaculture can improve food security and nutrition by increasing the amount of seafood available for people to eat. If done correctly, aquaculture increases food production, boosts economic growth in coastal and rural areas, and can help keep waterways clean. # Data | Dataset | Description | Source | | --- | --- | --- | | Bathymetry (depth) | Charecterize the depth of the ocean | [General Bathymetric chart of the oceans](https://www.gebco.net/data-products/gridded-bathymetry-data#area) | | Exclusive Exonomic Zones (West Coast Region) | Martitime boundaries use for the creation of species distribtion lists per country | [marine regions](https://www.marineregions.org/eez.php) | | Average Annual Sea Surface Temperature| from the years 2008 to 2012 within the region| [Coral Reef Watch](https://coralreefwatch.noaa.gov/product/5km/index_5km_ssta.php)| Information on species' temperature and depth requirements were acquired at [SeaLifeBase](https://www.sealifebase.ca/search.php). ## Analysis Blue mussels are eurythermal and well adapted to temperatures of 5–20 °C, with an upper thermal tolerance limit of about 29 °C for adults (Matoo et al., 2021). For the oysters, the information is the following: - **Oysters:** * Sea surface temperature: 11-30°C * Depth: 0-70 meters below sea level - **Blue mussel:** * Name: *Mytilus edulis* * Sea surface temperature: 5-20°C * Depth: 0-60 m ## Workflow for Oysters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # variables for min and max min_sst <- 11 max_sst <- 30 # Reclassifying SST and depth data into suitable locations # SST reclassification matrix rcl_sst <- matrix( c( -Inf, min_sst, 0, min_sst, max_sst, 1, max_sst, Inf, 0 ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE ) min_depth <- 0 max_depth <- -70 # Depth reclassification matrix rcl_depth <- matrix( c( -Inf, max_depth, 0, # should max_depth be negative? max_depth, min_depth, 1, min_depth, Inf, 0 ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE ) ``` ::: ### Find Suitable Zones for Oysters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # reclassify sst and depth to suitable zones zone_sst <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = rcl_sst) zone_depth <- classify(resampled_depth, rcl = rcl_depth) # Combine to adhere to satisfy both sst and depth for suitable zones depth_sst_zones <- c(zone_sst, zone_depth) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Find suitable zones for oysters adhering to both conditions suitable_zones <- lapp(depth_sst_zones, function(sst_data, depth_data) sst_data * depth_data) ``` ::: ### Find suitable total area inside EEZ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Converting sst data to match suitable zones sf::st_crs(eez_data)<- terra::crs(suitable_zones) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Convert to raster eez_raster <- rasterize(eez_data, suitable_zones, field = "rgn_id") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate cell size cell_size <- cellSize(suitable_zones, unit = "km", mask = TRUE) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Use only the cells with value 1 as suitable in the total area suitable_zmask <- mask(cell_size,suitable_zones, maskvalues = 0) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Select raster cells by suitable zpmes inside EEZ desired_zone <- zonal(suitable_zmask,eez_raster, fun = 'sum', na.rm = TRUE) ``` ::: ### Create Map for Oyster Colored by EEZ Regions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create tibble z_tibble <- as_tibble(desired_zone) # Merge for desired zones to EEZ data map_1 <- left_join(eez_data, z_tibble, by = "rgn_id") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Creating a color palette to differentiate the regions color_palette <- c("#d0f0f0", "#5fb3c7", "#1f78a8", "#08306b") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Visualize oyster suitable area by EEZ region tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") + tm_shape(map_1) + tm_polygons( fill = "area", fill_alpha = 0.7, col = "grey30", fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = color_palette), fill.legend = tm_legend( title = "Suitable Area (km²)", position = tm_pos_out("right", "center") ) ) + tm_text(text = "rgn_key", size = 0.7, col = "grey20") + tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2, position = c("right", "top")) + tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), size = 5) + tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE) + tm_title("Suitable Oyster Aquaculture\nin the West Coast by EEZ", size = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ! The 'size' argument of `tm_scalebar()` is deprecated as of tmap 4.0. ℹ Please use 'text.size' instead. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The scale bar would be 1.3 times as large when plotted at the top and 1.1 times as large when plotted at the center ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Numerical Oyster Reprsentation within EEZ Regions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create a table for area by region and suitability map_1 |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(rgn_id, area, area_km2) |> arrange(desc(area)) |> mutate(pct_suitable = area / area_km2 * 100) |> kable( digits = 1, col.names = c( "EEZ Region", " Suitable Area (km²)", "Total EEZ Area (km²)", "Suitable (%)" ), caption = "Oyster Aquaculture by Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) in the West Coast", booktabs = TRUE ) |> kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Oyster Aquaculture by Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) in the West Coast
EEZ Region Suitable Area (km²) Total EEZ Area (km²) Suitable (%)
3 4373.6 202738.3 2.2
4 3329.9 206860.8 1.6
5 3091.5 66898.3 4.6

2 323.9 164378.8 0.2
````` ::: ::: # Function: Find Suitable Area for Marine Species ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Function eez_species <- function( min_sst, max_sst, min_depth, max_depth, species_name ){ # SST matrix reclassification rcl_sst <- matrix( c( -Inf, min_sst, 0, min_sst, max_sst, 1, max_sst, Inf, 0 ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE ) # Reclassify SST zone_sst <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = rcl_sst) # Reclassify depth rcl_depth <- matrix( c( -Inf, max_depth, 0, max_depth, min_depth, 1, min_depth, Inf, 0 ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE ) zone_depth <- classify(resampled_depth, rcl = rcl_depth) # Combine the two zones together depth_sst_zones <- c(zone_sst, zone_depth) # Find suitable zones suitable_zones <- lapp(depth_sst_zones, function(sst_data, depth_data) sst_data * depth_data) # Determine suitable zones inside EEZ sf::st_crs(eez_data)<- terra::crs(suitable_zones) # Convert to raster eez_raster <- rasterize(eez_data, suitable_zones, field = "rgn_id") # Calculate cell size cell_size <- cellSize(suitable_zones, unit = "km", mask = TRUE) # Keep cell area only where suitable areas equals 1 suitable_zmask <- mask(cell_size,suitable_zones, maskvalues = 0) # Use zonal function to sum masked result and eez raster desired_zone <- zonal(suitable_zmask,eez_raster, fun = 'sum', na.rm = TRUE) # Create tibble z_tibble <- as_tibble(desired_zone) # Merge for desired EEZ regions map <- left_join(eez_data, z_tibble, by = "rgn_id") # Create color palette color_palette <- c("#d0f0f0", "#5fb3c7", "#1f78a8", "#08306b") # Visualize EEZ map_species <- tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") + tm_shape(map) + tm_polygons( fill = "area", fill_alpha = 0.85, col = "grey30", fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = color_palette), fill.legend = tm_legend( title = "Suitable Area (km²)", position = tm_pos_out("right", "center") ) ) + tm_text(text = "rgn_key", size = 0.7, col = "grey20") + tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2, position = c("right", "top")) + tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) + tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE) + tm_title(paste0("Suitable ", species_name, " Areas by EEZ in the West Coast"), size = 1) # Create a table table <- map |> select(rgn_id, area, area_km2) |> arrange(desc(area)) |> mutate(pct_suitable = area / area_km2 * 100) |> st_drop_geometry() return(list(map_species, table)) } ``` ::: ## EEZ Species Function: Blue Mussel Utilizing the function created above, a map, as well as a table with the total suitable area depicted numerically, can be easily recreated for the desired blue mussel rather than recreate the lengthy process of manually inputing the inforamtion for sea surface temperature and depth. The function is called after EEZ species and used as shown: - `eez_species(min_sst, max_sst, min_depth, max_depth, species_name)` Simply Input into the funtion: - Oysters: * min_sst = 11°C * max_sst = 30°C * min_depth = 0 meters * max_depth = -70 meters * Species_name = Oysters - Blue mussels: * min_sst = 5°C * max_sst = 20°C * min_depth = 0 meters * max_depth = -60 meter * species_name = Blue Mussel - Output: * map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Verify function by using oysters oyster <- eez_species(11, 30, 0, -70, 'Oysters') oyster[[1]] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=1056} ::: ::: Figure 1: Map of the West Coast showcasing the suitable areas that meet several oyster's sea surface temperature and depth for aquaculture possibilites based on Exclusive Economic Zones. ::: {.cell tbl-cap='Table depicting the total area (Km^2) by EEZ regions in the West Coast for several oyster species.'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Make a table for blue mussel knitr::kable(oyster[[2]], digits = 2, col.names = c("EEZ Region", " Suitable Area (km²)", "Total EEZ Area (km²)", "Suitable (%)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | EEZ Region| Suitable Area (km²)| Total EEZ Area (km²)| Suitable (%)| |----------:|--------------------:|--------------------:|------------:| | 3| 4373.56| 202738.33| 2.16| | 4| 3329.90| 206860.78| 1.61| | 5| 3091.52| 66898.31| 4.62| | 1| 1395.73| 179994.06| 0.78| | 2| 323.91| 164378.81| 0.20| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Use function for blue mussel blue_mussels <- eez_species(5, 20, 0, -60, 'Blue Mussel') blue_mussels[[1]] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=1056} ::: ::: Figure 2: Map of the West Coast showcasing the suitable areas that meet the Blue Mussel's sea surface temperature and depth for aquaculture possibilites based on Exclusive Economic Zones. ::: {.cell tbl-cap='Table depicting the total area (Km^2) by EEZ regions in the West Coast for Blue Mussel species.'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Make a table for blue mussel knitr::kable(blue_mussels[[2]], digits = 2, col.names = c("EEZ Region", " Suitable Area (km²)", "Total EEZ Area (km²)", "Suitable (%)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | EEZ Region| Suitable Area (km²)| Total EEZ Area (km²)| Suitable (%)| |----------:|--------------------:|--------------------:|------------:| | 5| 6545.83| 66898.31| 9.78| | 3| 3910.14| 202738.33| 1.93| | 1| 3152.90| 179994.06| 1.75| | 4| 2938.33| 206860.78| 1.42| | 2| 2410.14| 164378.81| 1.47| ::: ::: ## Conclusion Using the Exclusive Economic Zones to map out suitable areas for marine species that have a high potential for aquaculture development in the west coast of the United States. The conditions for the species were determined by using the sea surface temperature and depth below, oyster with a range of 11-30°C and maximum depth of 70 meters below sea level, and blue mussels with a range of 5-20°C and a maximum depth of 60 meters. The area for oyster farming was found to be in Central California with a total of 4,373.6 km^2 and the lower bound being in Northern California with 323.9 km^2. As for the second species, the suitable location being in Washington with a total of 6545.8 km^2 and the lowest being in Northern California with a total of 2410.1 km^2. ## Potential caveats or future directions 1.
